summary: Acrivastine is a short-acting, second-generation (relatively non-sedating) H1 antihistamine, structurally related to triprolidine, used for the symptomatic relief of allergic conditions such as seasonal allergic rhinitis (hay fever) and chronic urticaria. It is often formulated with the decongestant pseudoephedrine. Because it is largely peripherally selective it causes less sedation than older antihistamines, although some drowsiness can occur. It is renally cleared, so it should be avoided in renal impairment, and it is dosed three times daily because of its short duration of action.
indications: Symptomatic relief of seasonal allergic rhinitis (hay fever)
Symptomatic relief of chronic idiopathic urticaria
Relief of nasal and allergic symptoms (in combination with pseudoephedrine for nasal congestion)

dosage.n: For adults and children 12 years and over

dosage.d: One capsule (acrivastine 8 mg / pseudoephedrine 60 mg) three times daily
dosage.n: When nasal congestion is also present

dosage.d: Use with caution; generally not recommended in the elderly due to renal clearance

admin: Take one 8 mg dose three times a day
May be taken with or without food
Avoid in patients with renal impairment because the drug is cleared by the kidneys
Avoid alcohol and other CNS depressants while taking it
For the pseudoephedrine combination, do not exceed the recommended dose and avoid late-evening doses (insomnia)
moa: Acrivastine is a second-generation H1-receptor antagonist that competitively and selectively blocks peripheral histamine H1 receptors, preventing the actions of histamine released during allergic reactions, such as increased vascular permeability, vasodilation, smooth-muscle contraction, and stimulation of sensory nerves that cause itching, sneezing, rhinorrhea, and wheal-and-flare reactions. Because it penetrates the central nervous system poorly compared with first-generation antihistamines, it produces relatively little sedation. Its short half-life accounts for the three-times-daily dosing.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to acrivastine or to triprolidine
For the pseudoephedrine combination: severe hypertension, severe coronary artery disease, and use with or within 14 days of an MAO inhibitor
relative: Cardiovascular disease, hyperthyroidism, diabetes, or prostatic enlargement (pseudoephedrine component)
monitor: Blood pressure and heart rate when combined with pseudoephedrine

preg: There are limited data on acrivastine use in pregnancy. Avoid use during pregnancy unless the expected benefit outweighs any potential risk; non-pharmacologic measures and better-studied antihistamines may be preferred.
lact: Small amounts of acrivastine may be excreted in breast milk. Use during breastfeeding is generally not recommended; avoid unless considered essential.
renal: Acrivastine is eliminated mainly by the kidneys, and its clearance is reduced in renal impairment, leading to higher and more prolonged plasma concentrations. It should be avoided in patients with renal impairment.
hepatic: Use with caution in patients with significant hepatic impairment; experience is limited.

major: MAO inhibitors - contraindicated with the pseudoephedrine-containing combination (hypertensive crisis)
moderate: CNS depressants (alcohol, sedatives, hypnotics) - additive sedation
Other sympathomimetics / decongestants - additive cardiovascular effects (pseudoephedrine combination)
Antihypertensive agents - effect may be reduced by the pseudoephedrine component
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food; food does not significantly affect efficacy.
interactions.alcohol: Avoid alcohol, which can add to drowsiness.
interactions.diagnostics: Antihistamines may suppress skin-prick allergy test responses; withhold for several days before testing.

monitoring: Blood pressure and heart rate when taken with pseudoephedrine
Renal function before use in at-risk patients
counsel: Take one dose three times a day, with or without food
It causes less drowsiness than older allergy medicines, but it can still make some people sleepy - take care driving until you know how it affects you
Do not drink alcohol while taking it
Tell your doctor if you have kidney problems - this medicine may not be suitable
If you take the version with a decongestant, avoid taking it late in the evening as it can keep you awake
pk: Relief of allergic symptoms usually within about 1 hour
Peak plasma concentration approximately 1-1.5 hours after dosing
Short-acting - effect lasts several hours, requiring three-times-daily dosing
Store at room temperature, protected from moisture
pearls: Second-generation, relatively non-sedating H1 blocker and an active analogue of triprolidine
Short half-life means it is dosed three times daily, unlike once-daily agents such as loratadine or cetirizine
Renally eliminated - avoid in renal impairment and in the elderly
Commonly combined with pseudoephedrine (e.g., Semprex-D) for accompanying nasal congestion - mind the decongestant cautions
No standalone openFDA monograph; data based on product/reference information
missed: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember unless it is almost time for the next dose, in which case skip the missed dose. Do not take two doses at once to make up for a missed one.
overdose: Overdose of acrivastine would be expected to cause drowsiness and antihistaminic effects; the pseudoephedrine component can cause agitation, tremor, headache, palpitations, and hypertension. There is no specific antidote - treatment is supportive with monitoring of cardiovascular status; manage symptomatically.
